Compute temperature percentile thresholds for each day of year (terra version)

Source: R/component_terra.R
calculate_percentiles_terra.Rd

Equivalent of calculate_percentiles().

Usage

calculate_percentiles_terra(
  r_daily,
  n,
  reference_period,
  window_days = 5L,
  filename = "",
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

r_daily

A terra::SpatRaster, daily resolution (typically the output of temp_extremum_terra()), with terra::time() set. Not the raw hourly raster.

n

Percentile (e.g. 90 or 10).

reference_period

Character vector c("YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM-DD").

window_days

Width, in days, of the window used to pool neighbouring calendar days before taking the percentile (e.g. 5 pools \(\pm\)2 days around each calendar day). Default 5L, matching the standard CLIMDEX/ACI convention.

filename

Optional output path for the final thresholds.

cores

How many spatial tiles to process IN PARALLEL (a ceiling, further capped by .safe_cores_terra() based on RAM available and a single tile's size). Default 1 (sequential – tiles are still used for memory safety even at cores = 1, just processed one after another instead of concurrently; see performance note above). Note: the NUMBER of tiles is decided independently of cores, purely to keep a single terra::roll() call's memory footprint bounded (see .calculate_percentiles_terra_tiled()) – cores only controls how many of those (already memory-safe) tiles run at once.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with 366 layers (day-of-year 1-366).

Details

Bug fix #1 (see NEWS): this function used to take the raw hourly raster, filter it to day/night hours, and compute the rolling-window percentile directly on those hourly values (with window_size expressed in hours: 80 for day, 40 for night) – while calculate_halfday_component_terra() compared the resulting threshold to a daily max/min. Because the daily extremum of ~16 (or 8) hourly values almost always crosses the 90th (or 10th) percentile of the hourly distribution, this made the exceedance frequency during the reference period itself massively higher than the intended ~10 already-reduced daily extremum raster (the output of temp_extremum_terra()) as input, with window_days expressed in days (default 5), so the threshold and the tested variable are computed from the same daily quantity.

Bug fix #2 (see NEWS): even after bug fix #1, the threshold was still computed as a rolling-window n-th percentile (terra::roll()) followed by a second n-th percentile of those already-extreme rolled values, grouped by day-of-year (terra::tapp()). This two-stage procedure systematically under-counts the true exceedance frequency (observed ~5.6 applied) – see calculate_percentiles() (base-R engine) for the full explanation and numeric illustration, which applies identically here. calculate_percentiles_terra() now instead pools the RAW daily values within window_days of a given calendar day, across ALL years of the reference period, and takes a SINGLE terra::app() quantile of that pooled sample per cell, per calendar day – the standard CLIMDEX/ACI methodology. This also removes the terra::roll()/terra::tapp() dependency for this function entirely (simpler, and no longer sensitive to terra::roll()'s argument names changing across terra versions).

Performance AND memory note: looping over 366 calendar days and calling terra::app() on a (typically ~100-200 layer) subset of the reference period for each is comparable in total workload to the single whole-series terra::roll() call used before bug fix #2, but touches far fewer layers per call. A single such call over a whole country's grid could still, in principle, use substantial memory for a large grid – as a precaution the raster is still ALWAYS split into small spatial tiles sized to a conservative, fixed memory target (see target_tile_gb in .calculate_percentiles_terra_tiled()), regardless of cores – cores only controls how many of those already-memory-safe tiles run concurrently (default 1: one at a time).
